author: claude
subject: Point 4 cannot fail closed; the assertion mechanism already does what it wants
body:
Agreed on the schema evolution, including keeping `metrics.p50Ms` rather than removing it. Bundles v1 through v4 are immutable and use it; a reader of a retained artefact must still be able to interpret what it contains. Naming the pooled variant and materialising `repeatability.medianP50Ms` alongside is the right shape.

**Point 4 is the one I would change.** A `doc-check` rule "forbidding a comparison document from using the pooled p50 without qualifying it" cannot be implemented in a way that fails closed. Nothing in a prose document marks a number's provenance: `doc-check` would see the string `5 475×` and have no way to know which statistic produced it. The best such a rule can do is match a literal, which means it passes silently on any figure written differently — the failure mode this whole thread is about.

**The mechanism that does work already exists.** `docs/traceability.toml` carries `[[assertion]]` entries that compute a metric and require the formatted result to appear in the document. That is what keeps "225 unit and integration tests" and "milestone 0.11.0" honest in `WHY_OVERMESH` today. Extending it to performance figures enforces the number rather than prohibiting a definition:

```toml
[[assertion]]
document = "docs/WHY_OVERMESH.md"
metric = "listing_hierarchical_overhead_ratio"
source = "harness/artifacts/live/0.11.0/performance-v011-v5-failed-campaign.json"
pattern = "{}× direct"
```

The metric is computed from the retained bundle using the normative statistic. If someone later writes the pooled figure, or copies a stale one, the document fails the gate — not because the definition was misused but because the number does not match what the evidence says. That is falsifiable in the way a prohibition is not.

This does extend the assertion mechanism in one respect worth naming: **assertions would source from retained evidence rather than only from the repository.** I think that is an improvement rather than a complication, since it binds published figures to signed artefacts, which is the property the document's own preamble already claims. But it is a change of kind and should be decided as one.

**One caveat on doing it now.** The listing figures come from a `diagnostic-not-baseline` bundle. Asserting a number sourced from a non-baseline artefact is defensible only if the assertion also enforces the caveat text travelling with it. Either require both strings, or restrict evidence-sourced assertions to certified baselines and leave the v5 listing figures as prose until a certified campaign carries them. I lean to the second: the mechanism is more valuable if what it enforces is unambiguously authoritative.

**On the counterbalanced ordering: agreed, with the step this project has needed at every previous mechanism.** Recording the executed order in each run is necessary and not sufficient. Recorded and unverified, it becomes another claim in the evidence with nothing checking it — the same shape as `claimedClientInfo`, as the withholding gate, and as the request budgets before they were declared in the contract.

Add the check: the campaign asserts that the observed distribution of per-case target orders matches the declared counterbalancing scheme, and fails closed on divergence. It is a few lines, it turns a description into a property, and without it a future refactor that quietly restores a fixed order would leave the evidence still saying `counterbalanced`.

The rest of the disposition I agree with unchanged.

Verification method: source review of `docs/traceability.toml`, `harness/src/doc_check.rs` and `compare_live_performance.py`. No tests executed; no cargo toolchain is available in this environment.
